fair_value.method: Blend of 60% sum of the parts (~$278/sh) and 40% forward P/E (~$271/sh), rounded to $280, on 3.95B shares. The SOTP is core auto ~$120B (~$80B revenue x ~5% normalized EBIT x 30x) + energy ~$110B + FSD software ~$60B + net cash ~$27B = ~$317B, plus optionality of robotaxi ~$500B and Optimus ~$280B, for ~$1.10T. The P/E leg is consensus 2027 EPS of $2.17 x 125x. Analyst targets (mean $397, median $415) are treated as sentiment evidence, not as a method.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.detail: Core auto $120B (cut from $150B because the Q2 op margin was 1.4% and deliveries are tracking flat to down) + energy $110B + FSD software $60B + net cash $27B + robotaxi option $500B (cut from $550B for the NHTSA Special Order and the EU vote slipping) + Optimus $280B = ~$1.10T / 3.95B shares.

methods.name: Forward P/E
methods.detail: Consensus 2027 EPS $2.17 (StockAnalysis, 2026-09-24; other aggregators ~$2.20) x 125x, a premium multiple for ~23% EPS growth plus autonomy optionality. The 110-140x range gives $239-304. The stock trades at ~171x today.

methods.name: Analyst target cross-check (evidence only)
methods.detail: 43 analysts: mean $396.94, median $415, range $125-$600, 20 at Hold. Not blended into fair value. It explains why the market median stays above fundamental value.

bear.story: NHTSA's Special Order leads to a Cybercab pause or a lengthy FMVSS 135 exemption process. EU FSD approval stalls well beyond December. Capex above $25B/yr is debt-funded while auto margins stay ~1-4% and deliveries are flat to down. The multiple compresses toward ~100x on ~$2.2 EPS.

base.story: Muddling progress. Robotaxi reaches roughly 8-12 states but with a fleet in the low thousands. The Cybercab ramp is slow while the regulatory question is worked through. An EU vote in December or in 2027 is possible. Energy grows and margins recover modestly. The narrative premium roughly holds and the stock ends slightly below today.

bull.story: Unsupervised FSD reaches customer cars and robotaxi scales visibly (thousands of vehicles, many metros). NHTSA resolves via exemption or rule change. Optimus demos land, and a SpaceX combination is framed favorably. The stock rerates well above the $498 high.

thesis_break_reason: About 16% below the $297 52-week low, which already priced a 1.4% op margin and negative FCF, and ~33% below spot. I lowered it from $260 because my fair value fell to ~$280, which puts $260 too close to plain fundamental value to be a clean signal. A sustained trade at $250 would most likely mean the autonomy thesis is impaired rather than ordinary 46%-vol noise: NHTSA forcing a Cybercab pause, a serious robotaxi incident, unsupervised expansion stalling, core auto turning loss-making under debt-funded capex, or a value-destructive related-party deal.

Macro, rates and AI-trade sentiment given beta ~1.84
reasoning: Round 2 revision. The supervisor file has no per-agent feedback entry or 'changes' key, so I worked from its disagreements, key_drivers and summary, and verified them with 7 searches. (1) Share count: I already used 3.95B, so there is no change there. (2) Consensus 2027 EPS is $2.17 (~$2.20 elsewhere), not my $2.3-2.5. At 125x that cuts my P/E cross-check from ~$290-320 to ~$271. (3) The EU FSD vote is not on Oct 6; December is the earliest, and only 7 of 27 states back it. My Oct 6 '+' catalyst was wrong, and I trimmed the robotaxi option value slightly. (4) NHTSA escalated to a Special Order on Sept 10, with sworn answers due Sept 30 over the missing foot brake (FMVSS 135). I had framed it as a distant Q4 audit. It is a near-term left-tail event, so I raised bear probability from 0.25 to 0.27 and cut bear price from $230 to $225. (5) I also trimmed core-auto value for the 1.4% op margin and flat-to-down deliveries. Fair value falls from $300 to $280, a blend of SOTP $278 and P/E $271. I partly disagree with the supervisor on merger odds. Its ~47% by May 2027 is at the low end of what I found: Kalshi has shown 61-74% by May 2027, and Polymarket 47% for end-2027 as the leading bucket. I keep the merger as a two-sided '?' either way, so this does not change the ladder. The net cash figure differs by source ($27.4B on StockAnalysis vs $34.2B cash minus debt/leases in the Motley Fool piece). I use the conservative $27B. Distribution: fair value remains non-binding within 12 months because TSLA persistently carries a narrative premium and analyst targets sit around $397-415. I lower the median from ~$365 to ~$358, about 4% below spot. This reflects the slightly lower fundamentals and the nearer-term regulatory risk, offset by robotaxi expansion toward ~12 states as right-tail fuel. It uses a lognormal with sigma ~0.51 (46% realized vol plus binary events) and slightly fattened extreme tails. Scenario mix 27/48/25 at $225/$360/$570 gives a mean of ~$376, consistent with the ladder. P(>=372) moves from 0.48 to 0.465. No option data or priors consulted.

revisions.why: Supervisor finding that 2027 consensus EPS is $2.17 (verified: ~$2.17-2.20), lower robotaxi option value after the NHTSA Special Order and the EU vote slip, and core-auto value trimmed for the 1.4% op margin.
Supervisor consensus-EPS resolution (StockAnalysis 2026-09-24), confirmed by a separate search.
Core auto $150B to $120B; robotaxi option $550B to $500B on the NHTSA Special Order (FMVSS 135 foot-brake issue) and the EU FSD vote slipping to December at the earliest.
NHTSA escalation is a near-term (Sept 30) left-tail event rather than a distant Q4 audit, and the EU catalyst has been pushed back.
Median lowered from ~$365 to ~$358. I kept the wide tails (sigma ~0.51), consistent with the supervisor siding with wider tails, and slightly fattened the far-left tail (P(>=93) 0.99 to 0.985).
With fair value now ~$280, $260 is too close to plain fundamental value to be a clean signal of thesis failure. $250 sits ~16% below the 52-week low. This is my own view, below the supervisor's $258.
